title: The Cosmoprof Report: What’s Shaping Beauty's Next Chapter
description: Discover the biggest beauty trends from Cosmoprof North America, including SPF innovation, fragrance growth, K-beauty influence and what's shaping the future of beauty.

The OGAKI team attended Cosmoprof North America in Las Vegas, where conversations with retailers, brands, manufacturers and suppliers revealed a beauty industry entering a new chapter. Our biggest takeaway is a noticeable shift in what the industry now considers innovation. Across the show floor, one message surfaced repeatedly: performance is no longer enough on its own. Today's beauty consumer expects products that deliver clinically backed results, elegant textures, meaningful differentiation and a clear reason to believe. From next-generation SPF and K-beauty's continued influence to fragrance's continued growth, this year's show reflected a market becoming more specialized, more discerning and more intentional.

SPF innovation emerged as one of the biggest conversations at Cosmoprof, fueled by both regulatory advancements and a wave of products designed to make daily sun protection more intuitive. The FDA's approval of bemotrizinol—the first new sunscreen active ingredient approved for the U.S. market in more than 20 years—signals new possibilities for next-generation formulations. At the same time, brands showcased multitasking concepts that integrate UV protection into existing beauty rituals, reflecting a broader shift toward SPF that is lighter, smarter and easier to use every day.

One of the most interesting examples came from Solésence, which introduced Scalp Screen Dry Shampoo SPF 45+ Sunscreen, a hybrid formula that combines broad-spectrum UV protection with the oil-absorbing benefits of a dry shampoo. Powered by the company's mineral-based Kleair™ technology, the formula pairs SPF 45+ protection with scalp-care ingredients, reflecting the growing convergence of treatment, protection and convenience.

SPF is no longer confined to traditional lotions and creams. It's becoming integrated into existing beauty rituals, meeting consumers where they already are rather than asking them to adopt entirely new habits.

Fragrance remains beauty's fastest-growing category, and Cosmoprof reinforced its position as one of the industry's strongest areas of innovation. In fact, fragrance sales are up 15.2 percent year over year, according to Jacqueline Flam Stokes, managing director of beauty and health at global market research firm NielsenIQ.

One standout was Dossier's award-winning collaboration with artist and actor MGK (Machine Gun Kelly). Lost Americana, which took home Cosmoprof's Personal Fragrance award, captures a rich, earthy and spicy interpretation of American nostalgia through a distinctly 1990s lens. The launch reflects a broader evolution in fragrance, where storytelling, cultural relevance and personal identity are becoming just as important as the scent itself. For Dossier, an affordable luxury fragrance brand known for its designer-inspired scents, the recognition signals growing consumer appetite for accessible fragrances with a strong point of view.
Korean beauty is becoming the benchmark for modern formulation, particularly when it comes to lightweight textures, simplified routines and sophisticated product development.

One example was Mixsoon, whose minimalist, ingredient-first approach drew attention for combining high-performance formulations with uncomplicated routines. The brand reflects a broader shift among Korean beauty companies toward making advanced skincare feel more approachable for the U.S. consumer without sacrificing efficacy. Their PDRN Collagen Tinted Moisturizer includes rice PDRN, collagen and peptides that plump the complexion and offer brightening and anti-wrinkle benefits along with a weightless veil of color; and it’s available in 10 adaptive shades.

Manufacturers referenced Korean formulation standards when discussing everything from sunscreen textures to skin care delivery systems, reinforcing that K-beauty is no longer a niche category, it’s increasingly shaping consumer expectations across the industry.

Cosmoprof’s findings prove that products must deliver visible results, justify their claims and fit seamlessly into modern routines. The future of beauty is decidedly multifunctional. Across categories, brands are embracing multifunctionality, blending treatment, protection, color and fragrance into products that deliver visible results. At the same time, retailers are editing assortments more carefully, while digital platforms continue to accelerate discovery and consumer education long before shoppers reach the shelf.
